Fitting is done in following steps. i) Wet the ends of the thistle funnel and delivery tube with a few drops of water or glycerine. ii) Insert the tubes through the holes of the cork gently with a rotary motion. While doing so, hold the tube near to the hole of the cork. This prevents from breaking of tube. Rotate the cork slightly instead of rotating the tube to avoid breakage. iii) At last, fit the cork having the tube into the neck of the flask'
To test if the apparatus is air tight e) The air tightness of the apparatus can be checked by following methods,

Preparation of Gases Pour some water through the thistle funnel into the Woulfs bottle or round bottom flask such that the lower end of the funnel is just under water. Raising the flask, blow in through the other end of the delivery tube. Water will rise in the funnel to a certain height. Quickly close the end of the delivery tube with your finger. If the water does not fall down, the apparatus is air tight.

Close the end of the delivery tube and pour a little amount of water from a beaker slowly into the thistle funnel. If the apparatus is air tight, water will not fall down into the flask. iii) If the apparatus is not airtight, make it airtight. iv) If the apparatus is airtight, then blow out the water inside the flask. The corks, thistle funnel and delivery tube should not be opened once the apparatus is made airtight.
Object: TO PREPARE CARBON DIOXIDE GAS AND TO STUDY ITS
Carbon dioxide gas is prepared by reacting the marble chips with dilute hydrochloric acid and the gas is collected by upward displacement of air since it is water soluble and heavier than air.
